questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with someone who is not drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights flashing or a siren on, you must pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers on the road. Do not drive too close to vehicles beside you.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Eliminates the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol level. While it may help you stay awake, it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before drinking that you will not drive.
Saying no if someone offers you a drink because you are driving.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing any of the above.
questions.explanation: The only way to avoid drunk driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions after you start drinking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: If you drive a heavy truck or bus, you:

options.text: Must be careful and respectful toward other drivers.
Can use your vehicle's size to your advantage in traffic.
Can expect smaller vehicles to get out of your way.
Are only responsible for your truck and cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be careful and respectful toward other drivers.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses can cause serious damage and injury in accidents. Their drivers must understand their vehicle's size and weight and treat other drivers, passengers, and cargo with care.

questions.question: A bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to break traffic laws.
Can get a ticket.
Will always get a warning.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: You are in a line at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you:

options.text: Can go through without stopping again.
Must stop at the sign or stop line before going.
Can slowly roll past the sign.
Can follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at every stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not let other vehicles pressure you into skipping this safety step.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but never exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles a full lane width. Motorcycles need room to maneuver safely, even if the lane looks wide enough to share.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Leave the road completely, then return to it when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the gas pedal and steer parallel to the road. Slow down gradually and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and steering with a small turn. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, you should use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers when you plan to turn.

questions.question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: Parking is not allowed on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the other vehicle is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a defect that could affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have enough money.
Drive slower than usual.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that could affect safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is repaired.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. Your full attention is needed for safe driving. Any extra activity can be dangerous.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus returning to the main road after it stops. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means a person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. Watch carefully to prevent injury.

questions.question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you may turn left safely. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop, if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear before you go.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right lane right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane as soon as there is enough safe distance between you and the other car.

questions.question: When a driver enters a public road from a driveway or private road, what should they do?

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: Drivers entering from a driveway or private road must yield to traffic already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The speeds you might drive in the area
The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe legal speed for that road. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. Always slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop.
